subject: chimpanzee
title: Chimps in Senegal Sharpen Spears With Their Teeth to Hunt

scenes.text: Some chimpanzees make weapons, and it isn't the big males.
In Fongoli, Senegal, chimps break off branches and strip the leaves and bark.
Then they chew the tip to a point with their teeth.
They jab the spear into tree hollows where bushbabies sleep during the day.
Scientists recorded 22 spear hunts. Only one ended in a meal.
And the hunters were mostly females and youngsters, not the big males who usually get the meat.

description:
At Fongoli in Senegal, chimpanzees make spears: they strip branches, sharpen the tips with their teeth and jab them into hollows where bushbabies sleep.
Researchers Jill Pruetz and Paco Bertolani recorded 22 spear hunts, with one success, and the hunters were mostly females and young chimps.
Should this count as the first non-human weapon?
first_comment: Only about a quarter of the chimps went through every step of making a spear. Smart or desperate?
